subject: Tranche schedule & swingline drawdown — proposal for annual commit (COB-2027-017)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Tranche schedule & swingline drawdown — proposal for annual commit (COB-2027-017)

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a concise tranche-based drawdown we think matches CobaltAI's usage profile and procurement cadence. Summary below (high level):

- Commitment: $1,200,000 annual prepay for Redwood hosted inference (text gen + embeddings).
- Structure: 4 tranches (Q1–Q4) with a 10% swingline reserve for burst capacity.
  - Tranche A (Q1): $360,000 upfront (30% of annual) — funds loaded into a wallet at contract effective date.
  - Tranche B (Q2): $240,000 scheduled drawdown (20%) — invoiced at start of quarter, applied to wallet.
  - Tranche C (Q3): $300,000 (25%) — ramp-triggered: released when usage baseline + 15% projected growth is met.
  - Tranche D (Q4): $300,000 (25%) — standard scheduled drawdown.
- Swingline reserve: 10% of annual commit ($120k) available for short-term overage; reconciled monthly and replenished from next tranche.
- True-up: quarterly true-up to reconcile wallet burn vs committed consumption; unused prepay can be carried forward within the contract year or applied to overages per the attached model.
- Invoicing: we can invoice per-tranche or front-load invoices with milestone credits; default is invoice when tranche is scheduled.
- Term discount: we propose a 12% multi-year discount if you sign a 3-year term with the same annual commitment.

Attached: tranche-model-v1.xlsx (simple burn schedule + calculator).

Ask: can you confirm whether Cobalt's procurement prefers invoicing by tranche or a front-loaded invoice + monthly reconciliation? If tranche invoicing is acceptable, we'll prepare SOW + DocuSign link and get Finance/Procurement details.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Subject: Re: Tranche schedule & swingline drawdown — proposal for annual commit (COB-2027-017)

Ben —

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few procurement questions before we move to SOW:

1) Invoicing cadence: Our default is PO per-contract year; we can accept tranche invoices but prefer no more than 2 invoices per year unless there's a front-loaded prepay. Can Redwood accommodate an invoice schedule of 50% at contract start, 25% mid-year, 25% year-end?
2) Refund / termination: We need language for unused prepay on termination (pro rata refund vs credit). Can you surface your legal team's suggested clause?
3) Swingline usage: How is the 10% reconciled operationally and on the invoice? Do we get line items that show how the reserve was consumed?
4) Security/audit: Procurement requires confirmation that audit logs (billing + token-level usage) are accessible to our Security team for quarterly review.

Procurement lead: Mark Hsu (mark.hsu@cobaltai.com) — I CC'd our general procurements mailbox above. If you can share a short SOW + draft invoice schedule (PDF) and the legal clause we can put into redlines, I'll bring to Finance next week.

Thanks,
Emma
Director, Platform Engineering | CobaltAI
emma.jones@cobaltai.com

Hi Emma / Ben —

Couple of operational notes to make sure expectations align (quick, non-legal):

- Swingline reconciliation: monthly ledger shows: starting wallet balance, standard token consumption (charged at committed rate), swingline consumption (charged at committed rate plus short-term surcharge if >reserve), replenishment events (tranche/ invoice credits). Example row: 
  Apr 2027 | Start $360,000 | Std consumption $40,000 | Swingline $5,000 | End balance $315,000

- Burst capacity: swingline is designed to cover short-lived spikes. If sustained > reserve for 2 consecutive months, system will trigger a throttling policy or recommend an emergency tranche top-up.

- Cost transparency: we support token-level logs, per-route latency & cost breakdowns, and will provide a monthly CSV export for your finance team. Attached is a small calculator showing how a 10% swingline affects monthly burn and remaining wallet.

Happy to run a 20-minute walkthrough with your Finance/Platform team.
